html:
A great earthquake that struck the Kantō plain of Japan just before noon on 1 September 1923, destroying much of Tokyo and Yokohama. Around 105,000 people died, most of them in the fires that followed.

The quake, of about magnitude 7.9, hit as people were cooking lunch over charcoal and gas. Fires spread through the wooden houses, driven by strong winds. In one open site in Tokyo where crowds had fled, a fire whirl killed tens of thousands. Yokohama, the great port, was almost wiped out.

In the chaos, rumours spread that Koreans were poisoning wells and setting fires. Vigilante groups, sometimes helped by police and soldiers, murdered thousands of Koreans living in Japan, along with some Chinese and Japanese mistaken for them. Military police also murdered the anarchist Ōsugi Sakae.

Tokyo was rebuilt with wider roads, parks and concrete buildings. The disaster also scattered Tokyo's cooks and their nigiri sushi across Japan. 1 September is now Disaster Prevention Day in Japan.
